chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 73 — The Moon Receives Its Measured Light
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic wording has been identified for the Astronomical Book, while the limited Greek fragments do not preserve this chapter in full. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all eight verses: the moon's wind-driven chariot, its measured light, its monthly changes, its first visible phase, and the division of its waxing light into fourteen parts. Numerical statements and the text's phase model are translated as given rather than adjusted to a later astronomical system. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: After this command I saw another command, concerning the smaller light whose name is the moon.
verses.study: The moon is introduced under a command just as the sun was. Its lesser brightness does not place it outside the Creator's ordered purpose.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16 — God makes the lesser light to govern the night
Psalm 136:9 — the moon and stars govern the night by God's mercy

verses.text: Its circle is like the circle of heaven. The wind drives the chariot on which it rides, and light is given to it by measure.
verses.study: The moon receives rather than originates its light in this account. Motion and brightness are both gifts assigned in measure.
crossReferences: Job 26:10 — God marks a boundary upon the waters and light
Wisdom 11:20 — creation is ordered by measure, number and weight

verses.text: Its rising and setting change every month, and its days are like the days of the sun. When its light becomes even and full, its light is one-seventh of the light of the sun.
verses.study: Monthly variation reaches an appointed fullness. The comparison preserves distinction between the two lights while placing both within one order of time.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:19 — the moon marks seasons
Sirach 43:6–8 — the moon changes to mark months and appointed times

verses.text: This is how it rises. Its first phase goes out in the east on the thirtieth morning; on that day it becomes visible and is for you the beginning of the month, on the thirtieth morning with the sun, in the portal through which the sun rises.
verses.study: The first visible phase supplies the month's beginning. Observation of light links the calendar to a recurring heavenly sign.
crossReferences: Numbers 10:10 — the beginnings of months are appointed times
Psalm 81:3 — the moon marks a time for gathered worship

verses.text: One half of it goes out with one-seventh part, while its whole circle is empty and without light except for one-seventh part of it, which is one-fourteenth of its full light.
verses.study: The new phase begins with only a small measured portion illuminated. The text describes growth from near darkness toward fullness.
crossReferences: Zechariah 4:10 — small beginnings are not to be despised
2 Corinthians 4:6 — light shines out of darkness by divine command

verses.text: When it receives one-seventh part of half its light, its light becomes one-seventh and one-half of a seventh.
verses.study: The fractional description treats waxing as steady reception. Increase occurs portion by portion rather than all at once.
crossReferences: Proverbs 4:18 — the righteous path grows brighter toward full day
Daniel 2:21 — changing times remain under God's authority

verses.text: It sets with the sun. When the sun rises, the moon rises with it and receives half of one portion of light. In that night, at the beginning of its morning and before the day of the month, the moon sets with the sun and is dark that night in fourteen and one-half portions.
verses.study: Near conjunction the moon is described as rising and setting with the sun while remaining unseen. Hiddenness is one stage of its ordered renewal.
crossReferences: Psalm 139:12 — darkness is not dark before God
Isaiah 30:26 — the lights' future brightness remains under divine promise

verses.text: On that day it rises with exactly one-seventh part, goes out and withdraws from the rising of the sun; during its remaining days it becomes bright in the other thirteen portions.
verses.study: Separation from the sun's rising accompanies visible increase. The waxing phases complete the measured light over the remaining days.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — lights distinguish times and seasons
Jeremiah 31:35 — the moon and stars follow enduring ordinances

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 73 turns from the sun's yearly course to the moon's monthly change. The smaller light also travels by a wind-driven chariot and remains under a governing command.
The moon's light is repeatedly described as given and measured. Its phases therefore become a lesson in received vocation: lesser glory is still purposeful glory.
The first visible phase establishes the beginning of the month, joining observation of heaven to communal reckoning of time. Darkness, first light and fullness each have an appointed place.

The chapter's fractional model divides lunar light into fourteen portions and describes its waxing movement in that framework. The translation preserves that ancient account without replacing it with later terminology.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — the lesser light appointed for night and seasons
Psalm 81:3 — the moon marks an appointed time
Psalm 104:19 — the moon establishes seasons
Psalm 136:7–9 — sun, moon and stars are created lights
Jeremiah 31:35 — the moon follows the Lord's ordinance
Sirach 43:6–8 — lunar phases mark months
